_comment: Offline data-plane backends for new services. The engine in core/ is always the API surface (and is what Nano runs in the browser); a backend is the real, cheap, permissively licensed software behind it offline, used only where the service's behaviour needs a real data plane (a registry you can docker push to, DNS that resolves, a cache you can redis-cli). The gate enforces `policy` on every manifest's `backend`. `recommended` is the default pick per upstream id; the agent may choose a different real backend only with `backend.reason` in the manifest, and may never replace a recommended backend with in-process (the gate refuses it). EXPANSION.md explains the rules.

policy.image_tag: pinned version, never latest; prefer a vyomi/<name>:<version> multi-arch mirror (as with vyomi/minio) so an upstream image disappearing can't break installs
prefer: in-process (pure Python in core/, zero extra containers)
one shared backend for the same capability across clouds
JVM or multi-process servers only for Max
policy.compose: container backends go in docker-compose.yml AND docker-compose.cloudlite.yml under profile `full`, with a mem limit at the tier budget and a healthcheck, and are listed in tests/conformance/hourly/ci-services.txt so CI, the gate and the hourly run start them

coredns.why: records resolve with dig/nslookup; zones written by the engine

mailpit.why: real SMTP: SES SendEmail and the SES SMTP interface deliver into a local inbox (UI :8025). Optional per-space outbound relay to the user's own SMTP server and optional inbound (local SMTP port or IMAP poll of the user's mailbox) feeding SES receipt rules. See issue #61.

nats.why: JetStream streams/shards/consumer offsets; already in the stack. Also the durable delivery path for push services (SNS, EventBridge, Cloud Tasks): a stream per topic/bus/queue, a durable consumer per subscription/target, delivery workers that really call HTTP endpoints, Lambda, SQS and email (Mailpit), with retry/backoff, dead-letter queues and FIFO dedup. The in-process engine keeps the API and serves Nano.

caddy.why: One shared gateway for every gateway-type service: real HTTP traffic on each invoke URL / listener, routes changed live through Caddy's admin API (no reload) as users create them, TLS, CORS, rate limits, JWT checks. AWS-specific parts (Lambda proxy integration, VTL mapping templates, Lambda authorizers, usage plans/API keys, APIM policies) are a Vyomi handler Caddy forwards to. Already in the stack.

logstore.why: One log store for all three clouds, in-process on DuckDB (same code as Nano): entries, retention, sinks/exports, subscription filters and log-based metrics, with each cloud's own query language on top (CloudWatch Logs Insights, the Cloud Logging filter, a KQL subset). Logs are data, so in-process is the real backend. Fluent Bit (below) is the agent that ships workload logs in; VictoriaLogs is the optional heavy store.

duckdb.why: embedded analytical SQL over local/MinIO files, zero containers

docker.why: Existing Pro Docker compute backend runs the real containers (Free/Lite get the control plane only). For serverless containers (Cloud Run, Container Apps, App Runner, ECS services): each revision is a real container with $PORT, the shared Caddy gateway gives the service URL and the weighted traffic split across revisions (admin API, live), and a Vyomi scaler adds/removes containers by concurrency with min/max instances and scale to zero (Caddy holds the first request through the cold start). Cloud Run Jobs / Container Apps jobs / ECS tasks run to completion with retries.

k3s.why: real Kubernetes API for kubectl; Max only, control plane below

mariadb.why: MySQL wire compatible, unmodified separate container

kafka.why: Apache Kafka KRaft single node (not Redpanda: BSL)

spanner-emulator.why: Google's open-source emulator; verify arm64 before use, else mirror-build

ollama.why: optional real inference with small local models; without it the engine returns deterministic canned responses

fluent-bit.why: Not a store: the real log agent, started on demand. Collects logs from Vyomi compute (EC2/GCE/VM on Docker, Lambda/Functions runs, ECS/Cloud Run/Container Apps containers, k3s pods) and any user container, and ships them through its NATIVE outputs (cloudwatch_logs, stackdriver, azure_logs_ingestion) into the logstore, so the real ingestion path is tested end to end.

victorialogs.why: Optional heavy log store for large local volumes (Max): single Go binary; each cloud's query language translated to LogsQL, so edge cases can differ from the in-process store. Loki is not an option (AGPL, denied).

victoriametrics.why: One metrics store for all three clouds: CloudWatch PutMetricData/GetMetricData/Metric Math, Cloud Monitoring timeSeries (aligners, reducers, PromQL) and Azure Monitor metrics map to labels + step + MetricsQL aggregations. Also the real Prometheus backend (remote write, /metrics scraping) for Amazon/GCP/Azure managed Prometheus, Grafana-compatible. Every Vyomi service pushes its built-in metrics (Docker stats for VMs, Lambda invocations/duration/errors, bucket size, queue depth) and logstore metric filters write here. Roll-ups (CloudWatch 1-min → 5-min → 1-h) are applied at query time (downsampling is Enterprise-only). Nano keeps a small in-process store with the same API.

vmalert.why: The shared alert evaluator: CloudWatch alarms (actions to SNS, Lambda, Auto Scaling), Cloud Monitoring alerting policies (notification channels) and Azure Monitor metric alerts (action groups: webhooks, email via Mailpit) are compiled to vmalert rules over VictoriaMetrics, so alarms really change state and really fire.

knative.image: Knative Serving + Kourier on the shared k3s (pin a release when adopted)
knative.why: Optional most-faithful backend on Max: Cloud Run's v1 API is the Knative Serving API, so revisions, traffic splits, concurrency autoscaling and scale to zero come natively. Needs the shared k3s (~500 MB) plus ~300-500 MB. Not Coolify (a second PaaS control plane, ~500 MB+, no revisions/traffic split/scale to zero) and not Fission (Kubernetes FaaS, function-first rather than any-container).

in_process._comment: No container: the core/ engine holds the state (SQLite-backed where it must survive restarts). Same code as Nano.

current_stack_audit._comment: Existing offline backends checked against the same policy (2026-10-26). Not changed automatically; each is a product decision.

issues.option: OpenBao (MPL-2.0 fork, same API) or in-process for Secrets Manager/Key Vault

issues.problem: DynamoDB Local license agreement (not OSI); unpinned
issues.option: in-process DynamoDB core (already what Nano runs)

issues.problem: ~1 GB image each, JVM emulators (~300 MB RAM)
issues.option: a slim emulator-only image, or in-process Pub/Sub + Firestore cores (Nano already has them)
pin versions (release.yml already pins the appliance's own images)

live._comment: What is actually behind each released service today (audited 2026-10-28), shown as 'Wired today' on the pipeline page. state: real = the resource really works; partial = some of it does; api = management API only, nothing behind it. Update when a backend is wired.

aws:logs.today: in-process engine, SQLite store; filter + Insights queries

aws:ssm.today: Parameter Store real; Run Command reports Success without running

aws:stepfunctions.today: ASL interpreter runs executions and calls Lambda; Wait doesn't sleep

gcp:cloudscheduler/v1.today: cron fires only on reads; HTTP targets not sent (#147-#149)

gcp:container/v1.today: no Kubernetes API; kubectl can't connect (k3s not wired)

gcp:iamcredentials/v1.today: real RS256-signed tokens, JWTs and blobs

gcp:redis/v1.today: one shared 64 MB Valkey; port not published, no per-instance AUTH

azure:app.today: real containers on Pro/Max only; no ingress URL

azure:dns.today: no DNS server answers (CoreDNS not wired)

azure:monitor.today: alert rules stored, never evaluated or fired (vmalert not wired)

azure:operationalinsights.today: workspaces only; no ingestion or KQL queries

aws:events.today: rules match and deliver to SQS only; Lambda/HTTP/other targets not delivered
